name: Purslane

schedule.notes: Loves heat — sow only after the soil warms. Surface-sow; light helps germination.
Snip stem tips; pinch flowers to keep growth tender. Cut-and-come-again indefinitely.

harvest.cues: Stems 4 to 6 in, leaves plump and succulent. Avoid past-flowering stems — they get bitter and stringy.
harvest.storageNotes: Fridge wrapped in damp paper 5 to 7 days. Best fresh; freezes poorly.

varieties.name: Golden Purslane
varieties.notes: Bred for upright growth, larger leaves, better flavor than the wild weed.

varieties.name: Wild Purslane
varieties.notes: The familiar garden weed. Equally edible — pull and eat instead of composting.

notes: One of the highest plant sources of omega-3 fatty acids. Slightly lemony-tart, succulent texture. The garden weed and the cultivated form are interchangeable on the plate. Bolts after flowering — pinch to prolong harvest.
